reference_access.title: Dynamics of genomic innovation in the unicellular ancestry of animals.

reference_review.review_notes: Actual primary genomic Results identify canonical type IV collagen in Ministeria vibrans. This corrects a blanket filasterean absence claim; it does not establish a basement membrane or a performed human-like structural role in the unicellular organism.

reference_access.title: A unicellular relative links aggregative multicellularity to animal origins.

reference_review.review_notes: Actual primary Results report increased expression of alpha type IV collagen among ECM-related genes during Ministeria aggregation. Expression supports regulation in that model, not a demonstrated matrix mechanism.

reference_access.title: Collagen IV and basement membrane at the evolutionary dawn of metazoan tissues.

reference_review.review_notes: Actual original evolutionary Methods/Results/Discussion inspected. Some ctenophores and homoscleromorph sponges show basement membranes; Trichoplax and Mnemiopsis lack organized basement membranes despite relevant components. Historical finding statements are retained with explicit corrections; the separate Ministeria discovery supersedes blanket unicellular absence.

reference_access.title: A unique covalent bond in basement membrane is a primordial innovation for tissue evolution.

reference_review.review_notes: Actual human NC1 mass-spectrometric results establish sulfilimine cross-links; peroxidasin performs oxidant generation. Other species and zebrafish peroxidasin perturbation are separate assays. The inherited universal conservation statement is retained with a DISPUTED finding review because the later PMID28418331 distinguishes ctenophore cysteine-loop cross-links and the Hydra exception.

reference_access.title: Anti-angiogenic cues from vascular basement membrane collagen.

reference_review.review_notes: Identifier/title and complete abstract authenticated from genuine Europe PMC CORE metadata after the normal PMID fetch returned HTTP400. Abstract cache is mechanically rendered from that record, not authored. Selected original author-uploaded Methods/Results were read at https://www.researchgate.net/publication/12506976_Anti-angiogenic_cues_from_vascular_basement_membrane_collagen . Human placental, bacterial tagged and 293-produced preparations, CPAE whole-cell binding, HUVEC antibody-controlled attachment and HSPG ELISA are distinguished; no downloaded PDF/pixel claim.

reference_access.title: Characterization of the anti-angiogenic properties of arresten, an alpha1beta1 integrin-dependent collagen-derived tumor suppressor.

reference_review.review_notes: Original Methods/Results inspected: tagged human arresten expressed in E. coli, denatured/refolded, with polymyxin B control; calf/human endothelial cells and mouse alpha1-integrin-null comparisons. Positive cell-based ligand/angiogenesis evidence is independent of the retracted 2005 paper; repeated detailed signaling citations are not independent replication. Arr-2 is called last 115 residues in Methods and last 113 in Results/Discussion.

reference_access.title: Human alpha1 type IV collagen NC1 domain exhibits distinct antiangiogenic activity mediated by alpha1beta1 integrin.

reference_review.review_notes: Correct original article identity, but the entire paper was retracted in PMID:31895054 after notification of falsified data. Retained solely to document invalidation; no receptor-affinity, co-IP, FAK–MAPK–HIF or other positive mechanism is taken from it.

reference_access.title: Human α1 type IV collagen NC1 domain exhibits distinct antiangiogenic activity mediated by α1β1 integrin.

reference_review.review_notes: Genuine publisher full retraction notice read at https://www.jci.org/articles/view/135305 . It retracts the entire 2005 article after ORI notification of falsified data, without a figure-specific exemption. Normal cache remains abstract-only; full notice access is separately archived.

reference_access.title: Type I collagen gel modulates extracellular matrix synthesis and deposition by tracheal epithelial cells.

reference_review.review_notes: Complete original abstract read. Rat tracheal epithelial differentiation on type I collagen gel accompanies changes in alpha1 type IV collagen expression; full donor paper unavailable. Current donor IEP is not represented as a resolved target-performed differentiation mechanism.

functional_isoforms.name: Arresten / alpha1(IV) NC1-derived fragment
functional_isoforms.description: Arresten is the NC1-derived cleavage-product class, distinct from the matrix-forming precursor. The UniProt mapping describes the 225-residue arresten chain in the 1669-residue reference protein. Experimentally applied human arresten preparations engage endothelial cell-surface alpha1beta1 integrin and inhibit angiogenic responses. The 2000 recombinant construct starts at the SVDH sequence at residue 1441 and contains vector-derived residues; the 2008 preparations include tagged, denatured/refolded recombinant NC1 material and separate half-domain constructs. Those experiments are not all assays of an untagged native 1445-1669 chain, and they do not establish endogenous fragment concentrations. The 519-residue alternative splice product lacks NC1 and is not included in this functional class.
